source_verification_receipts.version: accepted manuscript corresponding to IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 64 (2018), 7264–7286
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives finite-sample concentration for AMP with iid Gaussian measurement matrices, rather than an aggregate fluctuation CLT for Causal-MP.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 119 (2024), 2178–2189
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops causal inference for subject-level derived outcomes in a hierarchical data-generating setting, including inverse-propensity estimation and multiple testing.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1212.6906v5, corresponding to Annals of Statistics 41 (2013), 2786–2819
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper establishes Gaussian approximation and conditional Gaussian multiplier approximation for maxima of sums of independent high-dimensional random vectors.
The article establishes AMP state-evolution universality over broader random-matrix ensembles via tensor-network arguments.
The preprint studies AMP for general non-symmetric random matrices with variance and covariance profiles; its stated focus is first-order tracking of iterate statistics.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define a single joint limiting experiment for (Z_m,Z_v,𝔾_{0X})—including all cross-covariances—and set Ω_θ as the covariance of DΨ_T applied to that joint vector; then define the sample analogue against precisely that target.

State and prove a direct asymptotic linear representation for θ̂_T using an observable row-level influence contribution, rather than combining a Gaussian limit symbol with a P_ξ expectation; this also makes Ω̂_θ consistency checkable.

Add a concise second-order-AMP literature paragraph distinguishing known first-order state evolution, nonasymptotic leave-one-out control, and any closest fluctuation results from the reused-matrix causal covariance claim.
